note: Rewritten from Hill (1927), where the species is placed in Calotermes (Neotermes); only the alate and soldier are described, the measurement table is badly OCR-damaged and not reproduced; plates and distribution records omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with head, anterior three-fourths of pronotum and abdomen auburn, posterior fourth of pronotum and apical margins of abdominal tergites 2–6 darker, meso- and metanotum, tibiae and tarsi dark brown; soldier with orange-rufous head above and reduced compound eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Antennae, labrum and dorsal surface of head orange rufous; frons and ventral surface ochraceous orange; anteclypeus hyaline suffused with orange; base of mandibles, external mandibular articulation and antennal carinae very dark; pronotum yellow ochre with a narrow brown margin; tibiae and tarsi brown. Head widest in the middle, sides slightly rounded, hind margin very broadly rounded, frons concave and slightly rugose, sloping gradually to the clypeus; clypeus short, about three-fifths the width of the head at its widest; anteclypeus as wide as the labrum; labrum markedly convex, rounded in front and on the sides; mandibles long and stout, left with two angular teeth near the apex and several smaller ones towards the base, right with a short broad tooth in the middle and another near the base; eyes hyaline and rudimentary, situated immediately behind the antennal fossae; antennae 14–17-jointed, generally 16-jointed, first segment one-third longer than wide at the apex, second half as long as the first, third as long and wide as the second, fourth shortest, segments 5–7 globose, 8–13 moniliform, 14–17 progressively narrower, seventeenth very short; pronotum a little narrower than the head, anterior and posterior margins almost truncate, sides rounded; legs moderately stout; cerci present in all 30 specimens examined.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head twice as long as wide, front slightly concave and rugose, with very scanty pale setae; eyes large, nearly circular, prominent and coarsely faceted, separated from the lower margin of the head by a space equal to half their height; ocelli large, broadly oval, contiguous with the eyes; postclypeus short, about three times wider than long, with four stout reddish setae; anteclypeus about four times wider than long, anterior margin truncate, yellow ochre; labrum brown, narrow at the base, rounded at the sides to the truncate apex; antennae 17- or 18-jointed, first short and broad, narrowed in the middle, second half as long as the first, third about as long as the second, fourth globose, fifth to fifteenth progressively longer, sixteenth and seventeenth equal to the fifteenth in length but narrower, eighteenth markedly shorter and narrower; pronotum with concave anterior margin, slightly rounded sides and slightly emarginate posterior margin; wing stumps large, covering two-thirds of the hindwing stumps.
